description: Machine-readable registry of CI-pinned documentation behavior claims for the Rust engine (the engine-neutral mechanism of the Java repo's ADR-0023). Each claim states exactly what its named engine test pins - no more. The claim's normative sentence must appear on one of its pages (scripts/check-doc-claims.py: whitespace-normalized, case-insensitive containment) and the engine test pin must exist as a fn definition; the pinned tests run in the normal cargo test --workspace build. An AI agent may treat these claims as source-verified.

claims.claim: The error dataset of an exception handler exposes the failing status as error.code.
claims.quote: error.code - the status code of the exception

claims.claim: A decision task branches on true/false or a 1-based integer; an integer above the branch count aborts the flow.
claims.quote: `true`→next[0]/`false`→next[1]; or numeric 1-indexed, multi-way

claims.claim: A non-boolean, non-numeric decision value coerces to 1 and silently selects the first branch; a missing decision aborts the flow.
claims.quote: silently select the first branch

claims.claim: A flows.yaml manifest that omits 'location' loads its flow files from classpath:/flows/.
claims.quote: `location` inside the manifest defaults to `classpath:/flows/`

claims.claim: A task-level ttl on a flow:// task makes the child time out first, so its 408 is catchable by the parent's exception handler.
claims.quote: overrides the propagated parent TTL so the sub-flow's timeout is catchable

claims.claim: An unhandled flow error reaches the caller as {type: error, status, message} with the matching HTTP status.
claims.quote: the flow aborts and the caller receives the error as

claims.claim: Registering a duplicate route does not fail the application: the earlier registration is reloaded and the newest function serves.
claims.quote: a duplicate route RELOADS the existing one, exactly like Java `Platform.register`

claims.claim: With env_instances, the configured value beats the annotation's instances literal when the key is set; a missing key falls back to the literal.
claims.quote: the instance count is configuration-driven — the literal loses to the configured value when the key is set

claims.claim: rest.yaml's stream: true is parsed by the engine and streaming replies ride a dedicated ordered reply lane.
claims.quote: Add `stream: true` to the endpoint definition in rest.yaml

claims.claim: A value in the runtime override registry (the -Dkey=value mechanism) beats the same key's configuration-file value.
claims.quote: win over configuration-file values

claims.claim: Configuration files merge in the manifest order - a later manifest file's value overrides an earlier one's, and keys unique to one file survive the merge.
claims.quote: merge in the manifest order

claims.claim: Envelope bodies are typed through serde on set_body/body_as - a small i64 round-trips as i64 with no Java-style Integer downcast surprise.
claims.quote: typed values pass through `serde` on `set_body`/`body_as`

claims.claim: Trace annotation and context calls are silent no-ops outside a trace bracket.
claims.quote: outside a trace both calls are no-ops

claims.claim: The Playground inspect command resolves whole subtrees, not only leaf keys.
claims.quote: a whole namespace: input | output | model | error

claims.claim: Export validates the declared root name only when one is declared; a missing or blank root name is accepted and self-named.
claims.quote: missing or blank root name is accepted

claims.claim: A graph whose root node lacks a purpose fails the CompileGraph deployment gate.
claims.quote: structure, the root node's `purpose`, data-mapping syntax

claims.claim: The reserved model-metadata key set is exactly ten names: cid, instance, flow, ttl, trace, parent, root, none, run, iteration_index - and every one is rejected as a data-mapping write target.
claims.quote: The ten reserved model-metadata keys

claims.claim: A graph is deployed only when manifest-listed and passing CompileGraph; a failed or unlisted graph is absent from the executable registry.
claims.quote: A graph that fails the gate, or is not listed

claims.claim: A suspended run replies HTTP 200 with {type: suspended, cid} - the run completed normally by suspending.
claims.quote: the run completed normally by suspending

claims.claim: A missing flow:// target aborts the run before any call and is not exception=-routable; a missing graph id surfaces as the delegate's 404 reply, catchable by the exception= route.
claims.quote: a missing `flow://{flow-id}` aborts the run *before* any call is made

claims.claim: In a MiniGraph data mapping a source that resolves to null (a missing key, or a plugin returning null) clears a model.* target (removed, or set to null when the source key exists or the target is indexed) and leaves any other target untouched - the same rule as Event Script - so a default for a model variable must come from the source side, never from default-then-overlay.
claims.quote: A null source clears a `model.*` target and leaves any other target untouched

claims.claim: On a schema.enabled binding a record that cannot be decoded (unframed, or an unresolvable id) is dead-lettered at once with the raw record, without a retry or a flow attempt.
claims.quote: A **decode failure is a poison message** (retrying will not help), so the raw record is dead-lettered immediately

claims.claim: The subject and version headers of simple.kafka.notification select the schema and are not forwarded to Kafka as record headers.
claims.quote: The `subject` and `version` headers are encoding directives: they never reach Kafka as record headers.

claims.claim: Linking the OpenTelemetry forwarder crate registers nothing; the distributed.trace.forwarder route exists only when otel.forwarding is true.
claims.quote: the route exists only when otel.forwarding is true

claims.claim: The OpenTelemetry forwarder exports each span with the engine's exact W3C trace, span and parent-span ids, so the backend reconstructs the lineage the engine recorded.
claims.quote: preserving the exact W3C trace, span and parent-span ids

claims.claim: The OpenTelemetry forwarder resolves otel.exporter.otlp.headers on every export, so a credential published after start-up as a runtime override reaches the backend without a restart.
claims.quote: The credential is re-read on every export

claims.claim: Stopping a flow consumer makes its member leave the consumer group at once, so its partitions are reassigned to the surviving members instead of waiting for the session timeout.
claims.quote: the consumer's close sends the group coordinator a **LeaveGroup**: the member's partitions are reassigned to the surviving members at once

claims.claim: On shutdown, after the consumers stop, the shared producer is flushed within a bounded grace so records callers already enqueued are delivered before the process exits; the handle is then forgotten.
claims.quote: the shared producer is **flushed** — every record already accepted by `simple.kafka.notification` or a dead-letter write is delivered before the process exits

claims.claim: In graph.math a boolean is never a number: a boolean operand in arithmetic, in a </> comparison or as a function argument - and a COMPUTE whose result is a bare boolean - fails naming the selector instead of computing as 1 or 0; an unknown function, an overflow to infinity and a division by zero fail by name too.
claims.quote: each enforced by a named failure rather than a silent value

claims.claim: graph.model.automation accepts a comma-separated list of graph manifests, each with its own location; when two manifests list the same graph id, the later manifest wins - its copy replaces the earlier one, and a rejected later copy leaves the id not executable (404).
claims.quote: accepts a comma-separated list of manifests, each carrying its own location, and when two manifests list the same graph id the later manifest wins

claims.claim: A deployment manifest's sets register all of a set's graphs or none: when one graph of a set fails the gate, no graph of that set is executable.
claims.quote: a set registers all of its graphs or none

claims.claim: A duplicate graph id that involves a packaged set is logged as an ERROR, and the later copy in compile order owns the id.
claims.quote: a duplicate that involves a set is logged as an ERROR

claims.claim: sets need an unpack folder of their own: a file:/ location the application can write; a classpath: value, the Playground temp folder, a folder another manifest uses, or no unpack at all skips the manifest's sets with an ERROR while its loose graphs still compile.
claims.quote: `sets` need a writable `unpack` folder of their own

claims.claim: A set whose entry is not named <graph-id>.json with a valid id is rejected before any file is written to the unpack folder.
claims.quote: rejected before any file is written

claims.claim: The generated manifest in the unpack folder records every file the loader wrote, and the next start removes the file of a graph a new version of the set no longer holds; no other file is touched.
claims.quote: the next start removes a graph a new version of the set no longer holds

claims.claim: The graph.math expression dialect is exactly: number, string and boolean literals; the operators ** (right-associative; a unary operand needs parentheses), unary + - !, * / %, + - (+ concatenates when either side is a string), < <= > >= (two numbers, or two strings compared lexically), == != (same type only, except that a string that is a canonical number compares as a number in all six comparison operators), && || (short-circuit), the ternary ?: and parentheses; the eighteen built-in functions sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, sqrt, abs, floor, ceil, round, log, log10, exp, min, max, pow, random (each also under Math.); and the constants PI and E. Nothing else parses: no bitwise operators, no assignment or user variables, no user-defined functions - an unlisted function fails by name.
claims.quote: This list is the whole dialect: an operator, function or constant not listed here is rejected by name, never silently accepted.

claims.claim: A graph.math DECIMAL statement is the high-precision COMPUTE: the expression is evaluated with exact decimal arithmetic and the result is stored as a canonical decimal string (plain notation, the computed scale kept, a zero of any scale written "0"); a Double or Float value is converted through its shortest decimal text at its minimal scale (exact over that text, and only as exact as the computation that produced it); rounding is always explicit, round(x, scale, mode); sqrt, log, log10, exp, trigonometry, random() and the constants PI and E are refused by name; COMPUTE is unchanged.
claims.quote: `DECIMAL` is the high-precision `COMPUTE`: exact decimal arithmetic whose result is a canonical decimal string, and `COMPUTE` is untouched.

claims.claim: In graph.math a string that is a canonical number (plain notation: an optional minus sign, digits without leading zeros, an optional fraction) compares as a number in == != < <= > >=, so '200' == '200', 200 == 200 and 200 == '200' are the same comparison and '9.5' < '10.25' compares 9.5 with 10.25; the comparison is exact, and text that is not a canonical number keeps the strict rules.
claims.quote: A string that is a canonical number compares as a number

claims.claim: In a graph.math DECIMAL statement a JSON number (a Double or Float) is accepted and converted through the shortest decimal text it prints as, at its minimal scale and in plain notation (5.0E-4 is 0.0005, 100.0 is 100), so a number and the same decimal written as a string give the same answer; it is exact over that text and only as exact as the computation that produced the number, which the guide declares so that sending numbers instead of strings is a conscious decision.
claims.quote: A JSON number is a double, and `DECIMAL` converts it through the shortest decimal text it prints as, at its minimal scale

claims.claim: In a MiniGraph data mapping a {namespace.key} reference inside a source resolves before the source is read - as a key segment (table.{model.key}), a list index (items[{model.i}]) or text in a constant or a plugin argument - and its value is inserted verbatim: a '!', '>', '&&' or '==' in a text constant does not quote it, and only a JSONPath filter quotes a text value; an unresolved reference renders the text null, so a composed key misses and the null-source rule applies; a composed key is case-sensitive.
claims.quote: A `{namespace.key}` reference inside a mapping source resolves before the source is read, and its value is inserted verbatim, never quoted

claims.claim: A $. JSONPath mapping source takes Jayway's result shape - by the kind of path, not the number of matches: a definite path (child member names and single indexes only) yields the value, or null when it is absent; an indefinite path (a filter, a wildcard, a deep scan, a slice or a union) always yields a list, one match being a one-element list and no match an empty list, unless a member name before its first indefinite step is missing, which yields null.
claims.quote: The result shape depends on the kind of path, not on the number of matches

claims.claim: A MsgPack payload the engine decodes - an event envelope, an Event API request, MsgPack.unpack - may nest at most 64 maps and lists, the outermost container being level 1, so an envelope's body may nest 63; one level more is refused as a decoding error naming the limit (Nesting deeper than 64 levels; HTTP 400 at the Event API) before the decoder's recursion can exhaust the stack.
claims.quote: A payload nested deeper than 64 maps and lists is refused as a decoding error, the envelope map being level 1

claims.claim: A MsgPack decoder of the engine - serializer::from_msgpack (the envelope and the Event API), EventEnvelope::from_bytes and canonical_packager::decode - refuses a header whose declared str, bin or ext length or array or map count exceeds the bytes that remain, as a decoding error and without allocating for the declared size, and refuses the format byte 0xc1, which the specification never uses; the shared vector file msgpack-hostile-header-vectors.json pins the same inputs in both engines.
claims.quote: A header that promises more than the input holds is refused at the header

claims.claim: Empty MsgPack input decodes as an empty map at serializer::from_msgpack and as an empty envelope at EventEnvelope::from_bytes, never as a decoding error, following the Java engine's MsgPack.unpack (the reference implementation), while canonical_packager::decode refuses empty input because a package is never empty; the shared vector file pins it as the control the event codec accepts and the canonical decoder rejects.
claims.quote: Empty input decodes as an empty map, so an empty byte array is an empty envelope and never a decoding error

claims.claim: A MsgPack payload the engine decodes holds exactly one value: serializer::from_msgpack (the envelope and the Event API) and canonical_packager::decode refuse bytes after the top-level container, well-formed or not, as a decoding error (Unexpected bytes after the value at offset N; HTTP 400 at the Event API), so two different byte strings never decode to the same value, following the Java engine (the reference implementation); the canonical decoder always did, the event codec does since Increment 165, and the shared vector file pins an empty map followed by 0xc1 and by a well-formed nil in both engines.
claims.quote: Bytes after the top-level container, well-formed or not, are refused as a decoding error

claims.claim: A root or end node's schema property declares the request or response in a closed subset of OpenAPI 3.0 keywords (type, properties, required, items, enum, minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum, exclusiveMaximum, minLength, maxLength, pattern, minItems, maxItems, nullable, additionalProperties; title, description, example and format documentary), and schema::compile refuses an unknown keyword, a keyword that does not apply to the declared type, a malformed value and a pattern outside the subset common to both engines, naming the location; the shared vector file graph-schema-vectors.json pins every accept and reject in both engines (Increment 172).
claims.quote: The vocabulary is a closed subset of OpenAPI 3.0 keywords, and the gate refuses any other keyword

claims.claim: When the root node carries a schema, the executor and the Playground's traveler validate input.body and input.header against it as the first thing at the root on every run through the built-in function graph.schema.validator (common::validate_input - an assumed step, nothing written into the node, never repeated by a resumed traversal); a failure takes the standard task error path - HTTP 400 with every violation in one message, or the root's exception= handler - and never reaches the root's own skill.
claims.quote: validated against the root node's schema as the first thing at the root on every run, and a failed validation never reaches the root's own skill

claims.claim: GET /api/openapi/{graph_id} (dev mode) answers a minimal OpenAPI 3.0 document of a deployed graph as a YAML attachment, ?format=json as JSON and ?view=contract as the derived contract with its evidence, and GET /api/openapi/session/{sessionId} the same for a session's draft; the document is derived from the model on every request and never stored (Increment 171).
claims.quote: The document is derived from the model each time it is requested and never stored

claims.claim: The graph contract (contract.rs) merges the declared schema over the surface discovered in the model (the path scan, direct evidence, one hop through a typed variable or an extension target's declared output): the declaration wins, a discovered path the declaration lacks is appended untyped and flagged, and a declared path the model never references is kept and flagged; the shared fixture graph-contract-vectors.json pins the contract view, the document and the describe lines in both engines.
claims.quote: The declaration wins: a discovered path the declaration lacks is appended untyped and flagged, and a declared path the model never references is kept and flagged

claims.claim: A Playground dry run validates the instance's input.body and input.header against the root's schema exactly as the deployed executor does - the same assumed step, the same message - and the pre-run check refuses a schema outside the vocabulary before the run starts.
claims.quote: A dry run in the Playground validates the input exactly as a deployed run does
